business_case.title: Business case: online booking and reminders for Tallowmere Physio's 4 clinics
business_case.decision_asked: Approve a 12-month Business plan for 4 clinics: $552 a month (plans plus reminder texts) and $750 setup, starting in November 2026.
business_case.the_problem_in_your_numbers: 62% of 2,600 monthly bookings come by phone at 4.5 minutes each, the front desk is paid for 35 overtime hours a month, 9% of visits are no-shows (about 234 a month), and 140 after-hours calls a month go to voicemail.
business_case.expected_result: Expected year-1 net benefit $34,597 on $8,184 of cost (range $15,352 to $54,668). Payback in month 2 (month 4 in the low case). 3-year NPV at your 10% rate: $102,466.
business_case.where_the_value_comes_from: At full use, $4,084 a month: fewer no-shows $1,551, front-desk time saved $1,371, after-hours online bookings $952, current tool retired $210. Revenue is counted at your 40% contribution margin, not at the visit price. All of the expected time saved fits inside the overtime already paid, so it counts as cash.
business_case.cash_view: Counting cash only, year-1 net is $35,407 and payback is month 2. It is $810 higher than the total because the cash view also leaves out the $810 of training time, which is paid time, not new spend.
what_is_assumed: Phone bookings that move to online booking: 40% expected (25% to 55%), seller customer data
Share of saved front-desk time that is really freed: 70% expected (50% to 85%), judgment
Relative cut in no-shows from automatic reminders: 30% expected (20% to 40%), seller customer data
After-hours voicemail callers who book online instead and would otherwise be lost: 20% expected (10% to 30%), judgment
Adoption ramp, months 1 to 3 (share of full use): 25%, 50%, 75% expected (low 15%, 35%, 60%, high 40%, 70%, 90%), seller customer data; full use from month 4
risks_and_how_they_are_handled: The biggest swing is the relative cut in no-shows from automatic reminders: year-1 net moves from $29,168 to $40,027. Year 1 stays positive even if the relative cut in no-shows from automatic reminders is 0: year-1 net would still be $18,308.
Even with no fewer no-shows and no after-hours bookings at all, year-1 net is $8,312, from time saved and the retired tool.

Staff adoption: the model ramps use over 3 months (expected 25%, 50%, 75%, low 15%, 35%, 60%) and the slow ramp is in the low case and the sensitivity table. Training is 3 hours per person and is counted as a cost.
Contract risk: 12-month term, and the current tool stays live until month 3, so there is no gap in booking.
business_case.how_we_will_check_it: Baseline now, check at day 90: share of bookings made online, no-show rate, overtime hours paid, and online bookings made outside opening hours. If at day 90 under 15% of phone bookings have moved online, the low case's level for month 3 (25% at full use x 60% ramp), we review the rollout together.

questions_for_the_buyer: For two weeks, count after-hours voicemail callers who never call back. It replaces the widest judgment assumption with your own number.
Can freed front-desk hours replace the part-time hire you are weighing for January? If yes, that time becomes cash instead of capacity.
Record overtime hours paid for the first 2 months after go-live. The drop shows how much saved time is really freed, which replaces the other judgment assumption.
